    Sanders: ‘Medicare for All’ will be HELP priority

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov.
    • Recent findings suggest that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen.
    • Industry observers note that democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Recent findings suggest that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders stated Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care blueprint if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

    Industry observers note that democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

    Recent findings suggest that sanders remarked Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

    In a recent development, his version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

    The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

    “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders mentioned, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

    Sources indicate that sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion blueprint, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

    While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of New York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders noted he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

    Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

    Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    In addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

    To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

    Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said last week that he plans to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

    Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee complications, he looks forward to finding common ground.

    #168545. Review: Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres (Hyatt Inclusive)

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2011 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Review: Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres (Hyatt Inclusive)

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Of note, I was in Cancun, Mexico for business meetings at another resort but wanted to evaluate both this experience for our readers as well as the overall position of Hyatt in its ever-growing Inclusives collection.
    • Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an adults-only resort in the Hyatt Inclusive Collection, and I toured it on a site visit in November 2026.
    • Address: Carretera Punta Sam – Isla Blanca, Mz 2, Lt 10, Costa Mujeres, Zona Continental Isla Mujeres, Quintana Roo 77400, Mexico.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Of note, I was in Cancun, Mexico for business meetings at another resort but wanted to evaluate both this experience for our readers as well as the overall position of Hyatt in its ever-growing Inclusives collection. My stay was almost exactly 24 hours and solo which is uncharacteristic at this destination resort. My experience will likely differ from other guests due to those factors.

    Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an adults-only resort in the Hyatt Inclusive Collection, and I toured it on a site visit in November 2026. It sits on a stretch of white-sand beach in Costa Mujeres, 12 miles north of Cancun. Cancun International Airport is the arrival airport. I could not confirm a single official transfer time from the property page. Tour listings commonly put the drive in a 30 to 45 minute range.

    Address: Carretera Punta Sam – Isla Blanca, Mz 2, Lt 10, Costa Mujeres, Zona Continental Isla Mujeres, Quintana Roo 77400, Mexico.

    Google Maps: Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres.

    Hyatt is the best in the business at high end resort arrivals. I had given my name at the security gate and by the time I reached the lobby, the door to the vehicle was opened for me, I was greeted by name and a “welcome home”, a constant refrain throughout my stay. It’s a small thing and maybe cliché but it was effective. I was given a Globalist upgrade even though rules at all-inclusives differ from the rest of the chain. As my upgrade was in a Preferred room, I was brought into a private room at the front of the lobby where check-in was done for me.

    The lobby is an open-air room under an arched woven ceiling, with a direct view out to the ocean.

    The resort is spread across 10 buildings with 505 keys. Of those, 221 are Preferred Club keys with an elevated experience. My building (and others like it) had just five rooms on each floor and just five floors which made it feel boutique rather than massive. Every oceanfront room is Preferred Club, and so are the first two buildings on either side.

    Sources indicate that the room views follow a simple rule by floor. Every first floor room is a swim-out, floors two through four are tropical view, and the fifth floor is ocean view or ocean front. That makes booking easy to reason through: if you want to step off your patio into the water, go low, and if you want the sea, go high.

    In a recent development, the walkways give a sense of grandeur and space. All of the flora is local, and in a touch I loved, the service rooms are named after the plants.

    There are four pools, and each one has a unique characteristic. The Jungle pool is drinks only and hidden in the middle of the resort by trees. The Social pool runs activities throughout the day at this adults-only resort for those who want to participate. There is also an infinity pool on the edge of the beach, and then the Preferred Club pool for those staying in that category. These are separate from the first floor swim-outs.

    The spa (hydrotherapy is included for Preferred guests) featured an outdoor circuit that included both hot and cold plunge pools, amongst other therapeutic services.

    The Preferred Club pool was the most frequented, though some images below look more vacant due to rain that rolled through during my opportunity to collect media on my short stay.

    The gym is open to every guest from 6 AM to 8 PM, and it is outfitted with Technogym equipment.

    Sources indicate that the spa is open 8 AM to 8 PM with 17 treatment cabins and a beauty salon, and hydrotherapy is included. That last part is the headline. The hydrotherapy space is ridiculous, easily the standout of the entire property for me, and it is the kind of amenity that would make me pick this resort over a competitor down the beach. There are indoor and outdoor showers as well.

    The men’s changing room featured private showers with an option for indoor or outdoor experiences.

    The theater seats 264 people and hosts cabaret and Mayan shows. There are also pickleball courts, which I am starting to think should be required equipment at any resort that wants a younger crowd as well as padel for the European set (and growing American interest.).

    Secrets is an adults-only brand, and every room here comes with what the manufacturer calls Unlimited-Luxury. For a standard guest that means unlimited dining and top-shelf drinks, Wi-Fi, daytime activities and nightly entertainment, with tips and taxes included. Add 24-hour room service, a mini-bar refreshed daily (you can ask for just about anything you want in there), and pool and beach wait service for all guests.

    It has been revealed that the Preferred Club is an upgrade, and at this resort it is a substantial one because it owns the oceanfront. Secrets lists personalized check-in and check-out, afternoon hot and cold hors d’oeuvres, desserts and premium liquors, access to the Preferred Club lounge and beach bar, an upgraded mini-bar, upgraded bath amenities, butler service, Bali beds at the pool and beach reserved for club guests, and exclusive dining at the Preferred Club beach restaurant. Preferred also gives club guests exclusive access to an infinity pool and puts an oversized soaking tub on the terrace of the upgraded suites (at least with the oceanfronts).

    According to recent reports, I book a lot of Hyatt’s all-inclusives through Hyatt Privé rates, and this resort is one of 388 in the collection. Privé is Hyatt’s invitation-only program for travel advisors, so you only get the benefits when an approved advisor makes the booking, and the stay still earns World of Hyatt points and elite nights.

    The all-inclusive version of Privé looks a lot different from a Park Hyatt booking. As I wrote when Hyatt’s all-inclusive resorts joined Privé, there is no room upgrade and no breakfast benefit, since every meal is already included. At this property, Privé guests receive a $100 resort credit per stay, a welcome amenity and letter, hydrotherapy access, and early check-in and late check-out based on availability.

    It has been revealed that elite status matters here more than at most all-inclusives. Under World of Hyatt’s terms, Globalists get the best room available at check-in, including rooms with club access, at the resort’s discretion. Explorists are eligible for upgrades too, but not to standard suites or club rooms. Travelers who have stayed at Secrets resorts as Globalists report being designated Preferred Club guests even when they did not land in a club building, which unlocks the lounge, pool and beach areas. This was my experience on all accounts at the resort. Late checkout is 2 PM for Explorists and 4 PM for Globalists, subject to availability at resorts. It was able to honor my request for a late check-out, I did not arrive early enough to request the early check-in. Hyatt waives resort fees on eligible paid rates (at least for now) and award nights for Globalists, and on award nights only for every other tier, and Globalists also get free parking on free nights though in 2028 Globalists will have to select this as a preference. One catch is that Suite Upgrade Awards cannot be used at Secrets resorts, so you cannot lock in a suite with one here.

    Weddings are significant business here. The courtyard outside the theater is the setting, with the sunset behind it, and the resort hosts lots of them. The resort disclosed its occupancy to me but it wasn’t clear if it was for public consumption. It was shockingly high especially for a Thursday in mid-November. Over the holidays or spring break all the hotels are full but this is a period where I would have expected a lull. Still, despite being extremely full, it never felt crowded.

    In a recent development, for meetings and groups, the convention space measures 9,800 square feet and splits into five sections. The boardroom was occupied at the time so I couldn’t include images of that.

    Recent findings suggest that restaurants can be booked in advance through the Hyatt Inclusive Collection app, which I wish more all-inclusives offered. Nobody wants to find out at 7 PM that the restaurant they wanted is full and through the app this can be done well in advance of a guest’s arrival. The dress code in the restaurants is resort casual, though the patio does not require slacks and closed toed shoes for men, shorts are acceptable outside.

    The restaurants include: Portofino (Italian), Bordeaux (French), Himitsu (pan-Asian, with sushi and teppanyaki), Oceana (seafood in an open-air setting), Barefoot Grill (light lunch), Market Café (the international buffet, which I noted on site as the Marketplace), Seaside Grill (a poolside grill), and Coco Café. The bars on that list include Rendezvous in the lobby, Barracuda on the beach, a swim-up bar, a beach bar, and the Preferred Club beach bar and lounge bar. There’s also a Sports Bar and Lounge next to the theater.

    Oceana is the seafood restaurant, set in an open-air dining room with woven pendant lamps, macrame hangings and a pebble mosaic floor. I chose this for my one dinner on property during my brief stay.

    I started with the lamb croquettes, which the menu serves with yogurt and sweet chili sauce, cashews, watercress and a pickled shallot salad, and the Iberian salad with fresh mozzarella, prosciutto, rucula, toasted pistachios, balsamic and roasted peach. A crusty loaf came with the meal.

    For a main I had the coconut shrimp, served with parsley orzo pasta, coconut sauce and parmesan crispy, and finished with the mango cheesecake, which the menu plates with vanilla cream and a mango compote with honey and basil.

    Market Café, the international buffet I noted as the Marketplace, serves breakfast until 11:30 AM. [TO CONFIRM: lunch and dinner service at Market Café].

    In a recent development, seaside Grill hosts the Preferred Club à la carte breakfast. The official dining page says breakfast there is served for Preferred Club guests only. I tried a number of dishes for lunch to report to our fine audience.

    Rendezvous sits at the heart of the property with 360-degree access, so you can walk up to it from any direction.

    Preferred Club guests get their own bar at the beach, and the Preferred Club lounge also has an indoor lounge for when the sun gets to be too much.

    My room was a Preferred Oceanfront King, a single open room with a king bed against a macrame headboard wall, rattan pendant lights, a ceiling fan, and a daybed sofa facing a marble bistro table. The balcony with jacuzzi looks straight over the beach. In the bathroom, a freestanding tub sits under a wood-slat ceiling beside a walk-in rain shower with a pebble floor and a bench. The double vanity has vessel sinks, round mirrors and a wave-textured wall, and the shower is stocked with Le Labo Bergamote 22 shampoo, conditioner and shower gel. Le Labo is a confirmed winner for me.

    I also had the chance to tour a master suites, all of which are oceanfront, and they are also available as swim-outs.

    Every first floor room is a swim-out, opening onto the pool.

    Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an incredible resort that somehow felt small when you were in your building but big enough to have everything. For my stay, I used 45,000 points on a no-notice booking to offset a $1,300/night stay. I have seen rates from $560 for off-season which is without question worth it. I loved the property and I look forward to returning with more time and my wife, but the adults-only nature of the property will make it a harder stay for us to achieve.

    What do you think? Have you stayed at Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres?

    #168543. Tech Report: The Best Places to Go in Europe in 2027

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 22m • 📚 Deep Dive (4393 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: The Best Places to Go in Europe in 2027

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4393 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that hoping to discover some of the best places to go in Europe in 2027?
    • We’ve asked our expert contributors from all around the globe to nominate the spots that are on the up—the places that are on their radar thanks to a flock of hotel openings, major cultural moments, talk of newly introduced flight routes, or concerted conservation efforts taking root.
    • From untamed wilderness in the Albanian Alps to the world’s oldest art fair (celebrating a big birthday in 2027) in Cologne, off to everyone’s latest favorite coastal coolcation destination in Denmark, this is our guide to the latest and greatest in Europe in 2027.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that hoping to discover some of the best places to go in Europe in 2027? No wonder: 2026 was a bumper year for European travel, from the Winter Olympics fueling a surging obsession with the Dolomites to the total solar eclipse bringing hoards of umbraphiles to the Balearic Islands, and celebrity weddings adding to an ever-growing love for Sicily. But as we edge closer to the end of the year, there are a few clear-cut destinations we’re most looking forward to visiting (and recommending to you, our fellow travelers) for the 12 months to come.

    We’ve asked our expert contributors from all around the globe to nominate the spots that are on the up—the places that are on their radar thanks to a flock of hotel openings, major cultural moments, talk of newly introduced flight routes, or concerted conservation efforts taking root. These nominations make up the Best Places to Go in Europe in 2027—and we promise they are worthy of your precious vacation time and hard-earned spending money.

    From untamed wilderness in the Albanian Alps to the world’s oldest art fair (celebrating a big birthday in 2027) in Cologne, off to everyone’s latest favorite coastal coolcation destination in Denmark, this is our guide to the latest and greatest in Europe in 2027. Happy travels. —Olivia Morelli.

    This is part of our global guide to the Best Places to Go in 2027—find more travel inspiration here.

    Go for: untamed wilderness and peaceful pockets.

    The Albanian Alp's village of Theth is a patch of pastoral living—and fantastic hiking trails.

    Local bed-and-breakfasts and guesthouses welcome trekkers, who do both day treks and through hikes connecting small towns.

    As Albania’s allure continues to grow, travelers flock to the Adriatic beaches of the south. But in the northern alpine region, the scenery offers a different type of drama—jagged snow-dipped peaks, turquoise rivers, hut-to-hut hiking—and in place of shiny seaside hotels, Albanian-owned wooden B&Bs welcome alpinists for home-cooked meals after long, satisfying days on the many surrounding trails. This area was largely isolated during the communist era, given its strategic location along the borders with Montenegro and Kosovo, which means that it has been slower to open its arms to the world (that’s also why you’ll stumble into countless abandoned bunkers from this period on your hike). The feeling here is that you can still show up to a guesthouse without a reservation, you can still camp wherever you find a spot, and, yet, there is also the sense that if you aren’t seeing this place now, or within the next couple years, you’ll miss the precious moment when it still feels like a secret to be let in on.

    Start your trip in the charming city of Shköder, known as the gateway to the Alps, where bikepackers cycle through the city, and restaurant patios spill over with guests enjoying glasses of Albanian wine. From there, many travelers strategy stops in the villages of Theth and Valbona (a stunningly scenic one-day through-hike links the two of them), or embark on ambitious multi-day journeys on routes like the Peak of the Balkans, which traces a two-week-long loop crossing into Kosovo and Montenegro. Infrastructure improvements have made roads and trails to access this region better in recent years, with much more where that came from. What was once only known by residents and those who purchased their paper guides now exists online, meaning it is also possible to base yourself in, say, the Eden-like Valbona Valley, and embark on a new route each day. Increasingly, there are elevated places to stay that preserve the soul of this place, opening in a slow trickle like Valbona Resort and Spa (2024) and SeSam Villas in Theth (2025). There may be folklore calling these the Accursed Mountains, but only because they are so vast and dramatic that their geography has historically kept intruders out. For hikers, that means a literal playground, with Albanian hosts leading the way. —Megan Spurrell.

    Go for: the next World Expo centered on play, and a booming hotel scene to match.

    Belgrade is set to host the World Expo in summer 2027, and a flock of newly introduced hotels will be ready to receive the travelers it is sure to bring.

    Sources indicate that all the world’s coming to Belgrade next year—and, it seems, coming to play. The Balkan city will host the next edition of the World Expo, a spiritual successor to the World Fair where nations come to exchange their latest and greatest cultural achievements and boldest ideas for the future. From May 15 to August 15, 2027, Belgrade plans to welcome over four million visitors to explore the theme of “Play for Humanity: Sport and Music for All." Its status as a host city feels especially symbolic as the Balkans emerge as a leader in technology and innovation across Europe. To meet the occasion, the city’s hotel scene is stepping up, with 15 new openings slated to cut the ribbon by the time the program kicks off. The crown jewel in the portfolio is the Ritz-Carlton, Belgrade, which will occupy a prime spot on the Danube riverfront. Other substantial names to watch out for include the InterContinental Belgrade and the Swissôtel Belgrade. In total, these projects will add roughly 1,500 to 2,000 new hotel rooms to the city. The shiny, new threads go well with the old in a place as historic as the Serbian capital, which lays claim to grand sites such as the Church of St. Sava, one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, and the Museum of Yugoslavia, which has a sprawling eight-acre park complex. —Kat Chen.

    Go for: a coveted summer destination at its sweet spot.

    A slew of luxury openings like Aman and Mandarin Oriental have arrived in Bodrum over the past few years, with NG Sign Bodrum and Bvlgari on the horizon.

    Industry observers note that for the past few summers, the glittering Bodrum peninsula has welcomed a wave of luxury openings, transforming this once-sleepy harbor town into one of the Aegean's most coveted corners. Aman, Mandarin Oriental, and homegrown Maçakizi were early champions of the scene and remain firmly at the heart of its appeal, but a upcoming generation of hotels, restaurants, and beach clubs has since made Bodrum one of Europe’s most sought-after summer escapes.

    It has been revealed that mayfair and Knightsbridge restaurant favorites Zuma, Bagatelle, and Novikov have all made the journey east in recent years, accompanied in 2026 by oh-so-chic arrivals from Dubai, Paris, and Marbella (Gaia, Gigi Rigolatto, and Maison Revka). Together they have helped recast Bodrum as a playground for the international jet set, bringing with them a distinctly cosmopolitan, see-and-be-seen energy.

    In a recent development, this summer also brought the long-awaited arrival of the adults-only hideaway Oku, the latest in the brand's collection of design-led retreats in Ibiza, Kos, and Andalusia. Throw in annual beach-club takeovers from the likes of Jacquemus and Alo, as well as boutique openings by brands like Cartier, and it seems there’s barely a name in luxury that isn’t lining up to plant its flag here.

    But 2027 promises to be the sweet spot. With fewer headline-grabbing debuts, the peninsula settles into a quieter rhythm, and openings such as Yahşi Bay’s NG Sign Bodrum, a villa hotel of sun-filled, glass-walled residences with two to six bedrooms, put privacy ahead of spectacle. It's the summer to explore Bodrum at its most relaxed. Reservations are likely to be easier to come by as last year’s hottest tables settle in for the newly introduced season and the eyes of trend followers will be trained elsewhere, leaving the regulars to do what they’ve always done: Dance as the sun sets on the wooden deck of Maçakizi, wander the meyhane-lined promenade of fishing village Gümüşlük, stopping for fresh seafood as they go; or hop between the coastline’s secluded bays, tucking into late-afternoon picnics beneath the pine trees.

    Enjoy it while it lasts. In 2028, all eyes will return to the peninsula as Bvlgari opens its sprawling hillside resort above yacht-speckled Paradise Bay, giving Europe's luxury travel crowd fresh reason to return. —Sophie Prideaux.

    Go for: Irish hospitality and spectacular sporting scenes.

    The 46th Ryder Cup will take place at Adare Manor in County Limerick.

    Designed by golf course architect Tom Fazio, Adare is nestled upon 840 acres of parkland.

    According to recent reports, home to natural wonders, ancient castles, lively pubs, and famously friendly locals, Ireland has long captivated travelers. While the well-trodden tourist trail takes in perennial favorites, 2027 will see another destination step into the spotlight. County Limerick, on the west coast, is gearing up to host one of the world’s greatest sporting events: the 46th Ryder Cup. Between September 17 and 19, the tournament will take place on the pristine fairways of the prestigious golfing estate Adare Manor. Designed by renowned golf course architect Tom Fazio, the championship course is set within 840 acres of magnificent parkland surrounding the estate’s 19th-century Neo-Gothic castle—a fairytale destination worth visiting at any time of year.

    Beyond golf, Limerick has a rich sporting heritage. Thomond Park, home of Munster Rugby, is one of the best-supported grounds in the world, with match days bringing a buzz to the city. Beyond the sporting calendar, there’s plenty to discover. Highlights include the 13th-century King John’s Castle, the Hunt Museum for its art collection including works by Picasso and Renoir, and Lough Gur, an idyllic lake beside Ireland’s oldest and largest stone circle. Limerick also makes an excellent base for exploring the Wild Atlantic Way. Around an hour northwest of the city, Lahinch is widely regarded as one of Ireland’s best surf beaches, while the spectacular Cliffs of Moher rank among the country’s most beloved landmarks. With world-class golf, a proud sporting heritage, fascinating history, and easy access to some of Ireland’s most spectacular scenery, Limerick is set to have its moment in 2027. —Camilla Hewitt.

    Go for: a city break that’ll stay with you long after you’ve left.

    In Cologne's Old Town, the charm is in the details, like this whale lantern outside Brauhaus Sünner im Walfisch .

    If you visit for Cologne's exuberant carnival, say as the locals say: “Morje es, wat do drus mähs!” (“Tomorrow is what you make of it!”).

    Sources indicate that let’s be honest: Cologne doesn’t necessarily win you over at first sight. It is not a conventionally beautiful city; rather, it is a feeling. Even locals will tell you that the city gets under your skin. Anyone who has experienced Cologne’s exuberant carnival spilling onto its streets and into its clubs and pubs is likely to fall for the city—and its people—for good. The motto for the so-called fifth season in 2027 is “morje es, wat do drus mähs!” (“tomorrow is what you make of it!”). Multiple crises or not, the people of Cologne refuse to let anything dampen their spirits.

    According to recent reports, and while folk culture is a major part of Cologne’s appeal, the city’s high culture is equally compelling. In September 2026, the opera house on Offenbachplatz finally reopened after 15 years of renovation—an occasion eagerly anticipated by many. Just 160 yards away is Kolumba, the museum designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Peter Zumthor. Its lofty, lime-washed rooms and the gentle light filtering through the narrow gaps between walls and floor provide a quietly dramatic setting for the art—and a welcome respite from the bustle of the city. Zumthor built the museum around the ruins of the former St. Kolumba church, incorporating the Madonna in the Ruins chapel by Gottfried Böhm. The work of two exceptional architects brought together in one place: that alone is reason enough to come.

    Recent findings suggest that the Museum Ludwig is another perennial draw. In 2026, it recorded its highest-ever visitor numbers thanks to its exhibition devoted to the late Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama. Art, in Cologne, is very much a capital-A affair. Every autumn, the international art world descends on the city for Art Cologne, the world’s oldest contemporary art fair, which celebrates its 60th anniversary in 2027. The 200th anniversary of Beethoven’s death is being marked in equally spectacular fashion. Throughout the year, the Cologne Symphony Orchestra will welcome a stellar line-up of renowned conductors and ensembles. The musical celebrations culminate in October, when pianist Igor Levit will take on all 32 of the great composer’s piano sonatas in a single evening.

    The city’s famously warm and open-hearted inhabitants are just as welcoming when it comes to gastronomic newcomers. Julia Komp, who became Germany’s youngest Michelin-starred chef in 2016 at the age of 27, knows this well. Today, her restaurant Sahila is firmly at the forefront of Cologne’s culinary scene. Other top tables include the intimate 20-seat Onda on Händelstrasse; Vunky on Eigelstein, specializing in plant-based fine dining; Toki, the city’s first kaiseki restaurant; and the recently opened Kluth, whose six-course surprise menu, “et kütt wie et kütt” (“it is what it is”), takes its name from a quintessential Cologne saying. —Ilona Marx.

    Go for: rugged landscapes and cinematic coastlines.

    Sailing yacht Orient Express Corinthian's itineraries will set sail to Bonifacio, Calvi, and Saint-Florent in 2027.

    Hotel Basgi Basgi is a favorite among design lovers in Corsica—a grow that is increasingly looking to the island.

    When Simon Jacquemus chose Phare de la Pietra, a 19th-century lighthouse on a rocky Corsican peninsula, as the backdrop for his Spring 2027 fashion show this summer, it was easy to see why. The designer, long inspired by the interplay of place, light, and raw emotion, described his show Le Bonheur (meaning “happiness” or “bliss”) as “a cliff that I add colors on top. An impressionist painting.”.

    It's true. Corsica is a place where cinematic elegance meets rugged natural beauty. It's why the island was once named Kallisté, meaning “most beautiful,” by the ancient Greeks. Here, dramatic mountains meet wild hinterlands and fiery red rockfaces jut against turquoise waters, making for breathtaking hiking through UNESCO-listed landscapes such as the Scandola Nature Reserve.

    Industry observers note that the island long slipped under the radar compared with neighboring Sardinia and the French Riviera. But Jacquemus’ arrival, coupled with a flurry of recent smart hotel openings, suggests that may not be the case for much longer. Leading the charge is A Mandria di Murtoli, a 10-room retreat spread across five restored stone buildings in the Ortolo Valley, which is a little sister to epicurean Domaine de Murtoli, where farm-to-table living is the order of the day. Elsewhere, Hotel Mylos on the west coast and Basgi Basgi in the north are drawing an increasingly design-conscious crowd.

    In a recent development, adding to the island’s momentum is the maiden voyage of the Orient Express Corinthian, a sailing yacht with 2027 itineraries calling at Bonifacio, Calvi, and Saint-Florent, opening up Corsica's fishing ports, medieval citadels, and spectacular coastline to a fresh wave of travelers. —Ashleigh Spiliopoulou.

    Go for: a coolcation destination with Michelin status.

    Newly-opened Betty Beach brings street food and brewery offerings to the beachfront of the Danish Riviera.

    The 60-mile so-called Danish Rivera is dotted with fishing villages, seaside resorts, and beaches.

    With rising summer temperatures across Europe, the Danish Riviera has emerged as the continent's favorite coastal coolcation destination. This 60-mile coastal stretch in Northern Zealand brings travelers the aesthetic appeal and culinary credibility of Copenhagen, but in a relaxed setting of fishing villages, sandy beaches, forests, and historical seaside resorts that remain largely undiscovered by international visitors.

    It has been revealed that the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in Humlebæk marks the southern end of the riviera, but many visitors staying in Copenhagen don't venture any further north to seaside towns. Many of the region's charming seaside hotels date back to the late 19th century. But a fresh generation of stays is rejuvenating the landscape with contemporary design. Cori in Hornbæk brings barefoot energy to a beautifully repurposed former hospital, and Hôtel de Ville in Gilleleje transforms an old town hall into an eclectic boutique spa hotel.

    Sources indicate that exceptional gastronomy abounds, with Michelin-starred standouts such as Jordnær, The Samuel, and Parsley Salon representing Latest Nordic Cuisine at its finest. For something more casual, recently opened Betty Beach combines beachfront dining, street food, and a brewery for sun-kissed imbibing. Denmark's first official wine route debuted last year in North Zealand and Odsherred, with nine wineries offering tours and tastings of cold-climate grape varietals such as Solaris and Rondo. —Amber Gibson.

    Go for: wild Austen-esque adventures and spa stays galore.

    Dartmoor's vast landscape, made of granite tors, walking paths, and moorland, brings the drama of Sense and Sensibility to life.

    Recent findings suggest that dartmoor has always lent itself to drama. Wild ponies pick their way through heather, granite tors loom out of the mist, and the ever-changing weather plays a starring role. Now it’s getting its close-up as the backdrop of Georgia Oakley’s new Sense and Sensibility adaptation in theaters in September 2026. The film was shot around Princetown, Tavistock, and Gutter Tor, and its release coincides with Dartmoor National Park’s 75th anniversary. As the Austen connection pulls focus to Dartmoor, 2027 is the year to stay a little longer and explore a little further.

    In a recent development, it’s unusually special in the depths of winter, when the weather gets wild. Picture misty mornings walking the ancient tracks and climbing tors, and afternoons yomping across moorland in conditions that demand retreating somewhere cozy for a hot bath and a roaring fire. For a hands-on experience, book one of the free conservation days running on selected Sundays in 2027 to learn more about Dartmoor’s prehistoric archaeology, wildlife, and rare species while helping to preserve its future. Don’t miss Tavistock, the old market town on Dartmoor’s western edge. Its handsome Pannier Market is bursting with antiques and curiosities, ideal for a spot of treasure hunting. For a change of pace, visit 11th-century Buckfast Abbey, where the Benedictine monks still make their famous tonic wine to a secret recipe.

    It has been revealed that to feel like a main character in your own period drama, book a room at Boringdon Hall. This show-stopping historical hotel on the edge of the moor combines roaring fires and old-world grandeur with one of Devon’s best spas. Its Michelin-starred Àclèaf restaurant retained its star in 2026, a quietly heroic achievement in a world obsessed with shiny fresh openings. There is nothing like spending the wildest part of the year getting wind-beaten on Dartmoor, then retreating for a spa treatment, proper grub, and a fire. —Zoe Cook.

    Go for: a hidden culture hotspot on the Iberian Peninsula.

    Évora, Portugal's prettiest city, is now home to the Vermelho by Christian Louboutin hotel.

    Évora's artisan traditions that helped earn the city its title as a European Capital of Culture.

    Industry observers note that although there’s really no need to do so—Évora is impressive in its own right—we sometimes refer to this little historic city as the Seville of Portugal. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986, its center comprises an imposing Roman temple, known as the Temple of Diana; a Gothic cathedral; the eerie Baroque Cathedral of Bones, next to the Church of St. Francis; and the Renaissance Palace of King Manuel I.

    In 2027, Évora will turn even more heads as one of the European Capitals of Culture. But Portugal’s prettiest city remains, overwhelmingly, a peaceful place, where at many times of the year you can stroll around in near silence. Then there’s the food. Restaurants such as Tua Madre, A Cozinha do Paço, and Forno da Telha allow you to discover recipes deeply rooted in the land and tradition. Don’t leave without trying porco à alentejana (clams and pork stew), ensopado de borrego (lamb stew), and a variety of local soups. And bread—plenty of bread—with superb olive oil. There’s also wine, of course, produced on the herdades (traditional estates dotted throughout the Alentejo region). After so much eating, you’ll need to get out and about. Which is perhaps why we find the concept behind Évora’s status as a European Capital of Culture so charming—the motto is based on the Alentejo’s cultural way of being: vagar, or to wander. —David Moralejo.

    Fuerteventura's volcanic landscape offers a stirring contrast to its surf beaches—and a unique draw for travelers headed to the Canary Islands.

    Boutique stay Casa Montelongo is one of several design-forward gems, this one tucked away in the charming village of La Oliva.

    According to recent reports, the second-largest and oldest of the Canary Islands, Fuerteventura is quickly establishing itself as one of the archipelago’s leading destinations. First came Paradisus by Meliá Fuerteventura, followed more recently by Zel Fuerteventura (the lifestyle brand created by Rafael Nadal in partnership with Meliá Hotels International). Set side by side, the two resorts form the Atlantic’s first wellness hub, set within a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Their privileged location on Sotavento beach completes the experience, with stretches of white sand and crystal-clear waters synonymous with the island.

    In a recent development, fuerteventura is also recognized as one of the world's best destinations for water sports, particularly windsurfing and kitesurfing. The area surrounding both hotels is home to René Egli by Meliá, a renowned water sports center. And beyond its coastline, the island continues to stand out. Charming villages such as La Oliva are home to a newly introduced generation of boutique projects, including Casa Montelongo, one of the area's hidden gems. With the spectacular Corralejo Dunes, traditional Majorero cheese, and dramatic volcanic and desert landscapes contrasting with idyllic beaches, Fuerteventura is emerging as the ideal destination for travelers seeking a holiday centered on sport, wellness, relaxation, and reconnection. —Maria Ángeles Cano.

    Go for: a vibrant city finally getting its moment in the spotlight.

    Beyond Liepāja's beaches, converted historic and Soviet-era buildings are a reason to visit this cultural hub in 2027.

    Plenty of the most seasoned travelers have never heard of Liepāja. That’s about to change: the Baltic coastal city has been named a European Capital of Culture in 2027, bringing a year-long program of public art, performances, and festivals with an allocated $11 million in funding. Curious visitors casting their gaze towards the little-known city will discover art-nouveau architecture, an atmospheric former naval district, and one of the longest urban beaches in Northern Europe.

    Industry observers note that it’s certainly smaller and considerably less visited than Riga, but the repurposed historic and Soviet-era spaces are strangely wonderful. Wiktorija, a former cinema dating from 1913, now operates as a multi-use cultural venue hosting everything from poetry evenings to rock concerts. Take a guided tour around Karosta, the former Tsarist and Soviet naval district, to explore the history of landmarks like the striking St. Nicholas Naval Cathedral. The Great Amber Concert Hall, meanwhile, is home to the Liepāja Symphony Orchestra, the oldest in the Baltics, which is already expanding its program ahead of 2027. Rooted firmly in the present rather than the Soviet past are businesses like MO Liepāja in Julianna's Courtyard, a cluster of restored industrial buildings along the Trade Canal now housing restaurants, bars, and creative outposts such as local surfboard maker Drtyboards. —Amber Gibson.

    Go for: a charm-packed city break, with upcoming hotels and gorgeous coastal scenes to boot.

    Naples will host the Louis Vuitton 38th America's Cup next summer.

    As for where to rest your head? Rocco Forte Hotels will open a 46-suite stay in the 16th-century Palazzo Sirignano.

    Gritty and pretty, chaotic and cultured, ancient and contemporary, Naples is one of Italy's most exhilarating cities. In 2027, the Campanian capital will host the Louis Vuitton 38th America's Cup (July 10 to 18), an event that has accelerated the regeneration of the industrial Bagnoli waterfront. Away from the waves, the hospitality scene is evolving, too. Rocco Forte Hotels will open its first Naples property, a 46-suite retreat occupying the 16th-century Palazzo Sirignano, restored by architect Michele Bönan, and complete with a rooftop pool looking out over the Bay of Naples and Mount Vesuvius.

    In a recent development, but Naples has never needed another reason to visit, with masterpieces such as Caravaggio's The Seven Works of Mercy and Giuseppe Sanmartino's Veiled Christ, and the antiquities of its National Archaeological Museum, whose forthcoming second site, Mann II, will bring thousands of artifacts out of storage. The city’s contemporary art scene continues to evolve at the Madre Museum, which recently welcomed internationally acclaimed curator Eugenio Viola as its newly introduced director. Nearby, Pompeii and Herculaneum agricultural parks remain as compelling as ever. And then, of course, there’s the warmth and spirit of the Neapolitan people.

    Da Attilio, Concettina ai Tre Santi, 50 Kalò, Diego Vitagliano, and Pizzaria La Notizia are practically compulsory for pizza, but there’s more to the city’s rich food scene. Donna Teresa and Mimì alla Ferrovia are among the beloved mainstays serving some of the finest traditional Neapolitan cuisine. —Jaclyn de Giorgio.

    Go for: an under-the-radar Ionian gem.

    It has been revealed that parga is the kind of Grecian destination every traveler hopes to find: easy to reach, yet seemingly under the radar. Latest hotels in 2026 and 2027 add to the appeal, without blowing its cover.

    It has been revealed that glittering Ionian water, pine-clad hills tumbling into a colorful harbor, and a Venetian castle above it all: Parga is undoubtedly picturesque. Yet this little corner of the Greek mainland remains surprisingly under the radar. Its old town is made for slow wandering, leisurely lunching on seafood or traditional Greek mezze at waterfront tavernas, and exploring seriously beautiful beaches such as Valtos, a gold sand bay with award-winning Blue Flag credentials. Inland, meanwhile, the Acheron River makes a heavenly setting for horseback riding, rafting, canyon walks, and swimming.

    Industry observers note that part of Parga’s appeal is how easy it is to reach: Tiny-but-mighty Preveza Airport is only an hour away, making this feel like a secret without the schlep. Parga Beach Resort, directly on Valtos Beach, makes a particularly excellent base. Its new beachfront suites, released in late summer 2026, sleep up to two adults and four children. A regular water taxi nips around the bay to Parga town, turning supper in that spectacular harbor into part of the adventure. The 2027 opening of Varko Bay nearby will add another high-end stay, with villas, a spa, sandy beaches, and a private marina. —Zoe Cook.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    How to avoid petty theft while traveling

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (134 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • Petty theft is a risk in many popular destinations, especially crowded tourist sites and public transportation hubs.
  • Travelers can reduce their risk by minimizing valuables, blending in with locals and staying vigilant in busy areas.
  • Using theft-resistant bags, securing belongings and splitting up valuables are effective strategies to deter thieves.
  • Travel insurance may cover some theft incidents, but additional coverage could be necessary for high-value items.
  • Thieves often work in teams, using distractions or disturbances to target unsuspecting travelers.
  • Scams can take many forms, including unsolicited offers of help or unexpected gifts that later require payment.
  • Leaving valuables in hotel safes or locked suitcases is generally safer than carrying everything while sightseeing.

    #168541. Industry News: Editorial: JetBlue Status Match Made Clear It’s Not For Me

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1342 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Editorial: JetBlue Status Match Made Clear It’s Not For Me

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1342 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Last June, JetBlue launched a status match that put elites from competing carriers into Mosaic 1 or Mosaic 2.
    • In a recent development, my application was approved just before the June 30 deadline.
    • In a recent development, my two primary airports are Pittsburgh, PA (PIT) and Fort Myers, FL (RSW).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Last June, JetBlue launched a status match that put elites from competing carriers into Mosaic 1 or Mosaic 2. It also offered a faster track for Delta Diamond, Delta 360, AA Executive Platinum and Concierge Key members: earn 50 tiles by year-end and get Mosaic 4. That worked out to $5,000 in JetBlue flights or Paisly packages, or $50,000 on the JetBlue card, and a single Mint roundtrip to Europe could cover most of it. I already had AA Executive Platinum, so I didn’t need the status. I wanted it anyway. JetBlue was adding routes from my home airports, I fly to Boston, New York and Fort Lauderdale often, and the United partnership raised the possibility of benefits on both sides.

    In a recent development, my application was approved just before the June 30 deadline. Some applicants waited up to six weeks for processing, though, and losing six weeks of a 12-week challenge is a real cost. JetBlue then added its 25-for-25 promotion on top. Visiting 25 destinations by year-end earned up to 350,000 TrueBlue points plus 25 years of Mosaic 1, which made a cheap, aggressive weekend of short hops look worth it. My initiative was to finish the challenge through spend and put the points toward transatlantic and Japan trips. My one worry at the time was whether JetBlue would treat these upcoming Mosaics well enough to keep them flying with it.

    In a recent development, my two primary airports are Pittsburgh, PA (PIT) and Fort Myers, FL (RSW). I occasionally also fly from Fort Lauderdale or Miami when it makes sense. But Pittsburgh had just flights to Boston for some of last year, before adding Fort Lauderdale to fill the Spirit gap and then New York JFK competing with Delta, and more broadly to the New York market, United and American with more than enough flights. From Fort Myers, it’s Boston of JFK.

    It has been revealed that I flew once to Boston on JetBlue but at the time, it had not yet launched a domestic first class, a better seat selection included in my fare was the only real enhancement to the short flight of just over 80 minutes. I’ll cover other reasons why I wasn’t able to fly the carrier more, but given that I am not in Latest York, Boston, or Fort Lauderdale full time, every flight I take has a connection and it’s not particularly on-the-way for me. For example, if heading south to Florida, Charlotte, Atlanta, or even Washington Dulles make more sense than Boston or New York but when heading west at all, Chicago, Houston, Dallas, and Denver are all obviously better options.

    Sources indicate that even to Europe, there’s not a material advantage with limited schedules and limited footprint on the continent. For trips to Paris given that I will have to connect anyway, I have more options on any other carrier through east coast hubs than with JetBlue on its metal not to mention partner networks.

    Recent findings suggest that most recently, I had a flight to Cancun and with airport time, flight time and connections, it’s faster to fly out of Miami or Fort Lauderdale. But JetBlue had fewer flights for more money and far more miles than with American. Outside of the northeast corridor or based in South(east) Florida, I couldn’t make it make sense.

    Sources indicate that I’m heading to Europe for a meeting next week and I will finally have a chance to try Mint. This will constitute two of my longest flights with JetBlue ever. I haven’t heard many negative comments about JetBlue Mint, and I have high expectations. It’s hard to get excited about another American or United flight in business class solely because I have flown those so often and there’s little newly introduced there.

    According to recent reports, I’ll get a chance to try a reasonably long three-hour flight domestically to see how it differs from my prior JetBlue experience. Then, assuming flights are on time, I should have a chance to try the latest BlueHouse, a first for me. Following that is a long haul flight in Mint and I am looking forward to the experience.

    In a recent development, statistically, I can’t see a reason that I try for Mosaic again, but who knows? The experience could change what appears to be a clear analytical decision for me at this point.

    Industry observers note that one of the biggest reasons I secure status via flying/spending/staying is to redeem systemwide upgrades (or suite upgrades in the case of hotels.) I’ll fully admit that upon receiving approval for the challenge last year, I hadn’t even considered that Mint certificates would work differently than other upgrade certificates in the industry. One upgrade certificate is worth an upgrade (if available.) United uses “Plus Points” but it feels clearer that there will be some variability in what’s required to move between the cabins.

    Sources indicate that for this particular trip, JetBlue wanted two upgrade certificates in one direction, and four on another. Thankfully, I had taken the upgrade option every time I achieved a choice to select a benefit, but had I chosen something else assuming that I’d only need two Move to Mint certificates (as I would with American for example) I would have come up short.

    I covered how much spending is required to achieve top tier status and its associated benefits in recent posts. This was in response to United’s move to require $480,000 in annual spending (by credit card only) to achieve United 1K status. Assuming that along the way loyalty points are taken and annual Mosaic bonuses are applied to cardholders, JetBlue is above American at $225,000 in spend for Mosaic 4 vs. American’s net of $164,000 for Executive Platinum with just two systemwide upgrades, or $214,000 with six. The difference is that those six upgrades apply for the full-one-way on a single certificate.

    Industry observers note that I spent time trying to figure out why one way charged four Move to Mint vs two and in the end, it didn’t really matter. I can nearly upgrade my entire family of four on American vs a single roundtrip for myself. For what it’s worth, the base cost was also more expensive with JetBlue than American for which I had upgrades available.

    According to recent reports, I have the qualified business spend to earn Mosaic 4 every year, but the value of its perks aren’t even close to the rest of the market. And for what JetBlue expects in spend compared to what I could earn elsewhere is uncompetitive.

    And as a side note, the fixed rate of JetBlue points (about 1.4¢/each) is unimpressive but for most of the attempts I tried to use them throughout the year both domestically and internationally, they proved of little value. A lack of partners is much the same. I looked at a redemption in Mint on my flights to Europe and though I had more than 220,000, it was an insufficient balance for the simple roundtrip. For context, I took United a few years ago on miles and redeemed 160,000 roundtrip (this year was available at 176,000 roundtrip) and multiple times in the last 24 months on American at or around 115,000 roundtrip. Miles aren’t worth enough, they aren’t flexible enough, and there aren’t enough partners to fill gaps in the JetBlue map.

    Industry observers note that I had higher expectations for JetBlue based on the experiences of my peers. I think its equipment is excellent, but widespread first class availability is a necessity. The limited utility of Move to Mint certificates were the nail in the coffin and the usability of the miles didn’t help. But even then, I really want to love and fly JetBlue, and I am willing to go a little out of my way to use them. But I’m not willing to fly backwards for fewer flights at a higher cost.

    #168540. 16 Incredible Hotels in Morocco Whether You’re Looking for a Royal Riad or a Kitesurfing Sanctuary

    📅 10 Sep 2025 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2895 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    16 Incredible Hotels in Morocco Whether You’re Looking for a Royal Riad or a Kitesurfing Sanctuary

    📅 10 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the gateway of Africa is chameleon when it comes to its cultural offering, and thus choosing the best hotels in Morocco is a varied task.
    • According to recent reports, right now the country is witnessing a transformation in tourism as it prepares to host the men's FIFA World Cup 2030.
    • Perched at the edge of the desert, Marrakech is improbably a garden city, its medina an intricate jigsaw of riad courtyards that reflect deeply held Islamic beliefs about water, light, and the art of living harmoniously with the natural world.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the gateway of Africa is chameleon when it comes to its cultural offering, and thus choosing the best hotels in Morocco is a varied task. Whether you’re looking for a charming riad stay in Marrakech, yearn for serenity and seclusion in the Atlas Mountains or blueprint to immerse yourself in the Agafay desert, there’s so more to this colorful country than the promise of winter sun. It’s perhaps obvious, then, why Morocco has long since been favored by the fashionable jet set crowd, and has become home to so many notable hotel addresses. Some are so lavish they veer on palaces, others are romantically reimagined farmhouses or bohemian beachside boltholes.

    According to recent reports, right now the country is witnessing a transformation in tourism as it prepares to host the men's FIFA World Cup 2030. One of the biggest changes is the multi-million dollar rail expansion project, which will connect Kenitra with Marrakech, via Rabat and Casablanca. On the hotel front, Four Seasons is set to open a new address in Tangier, while Virgin Limited Edition aims to open a hotel near Marrakech. For the latest and greatest addresses, here is our pick of the best hotels in Morocco.

    The pool at El Fenn in Marrakech.

    Perched at the edge of the desert, Marrakech is improbably a garden city, its medina an intricate jigsaw of riad courtyards that reflect deeply held Islamic beliefs about water, light, and the art of living harmoniously with the natural world. Jnane Rumi—the Garden of Rumi—sits squarely within this tradition in the Palmeraie, Marrakech’s historic palm grove. It was designed by Tunisian-born Charles Boccara as a private home and has just 12 rooms: 7 in the mansion, 4 garden pavilions, and 1 private villa. Boccara grew up in Casablanca and graduated from the Beaux-Arts de Paris, and this mini manor house—with its arches and domes, expressive use of local materials, and elegantly ­mullioned windows that connect the house with a glorious garden of centenarian palms and pistachio trees—embodies his elegant Euro-Maghrebi style. It’s a seductive oasis that ­naturally gathers life, which is why owners Gert-Jan van den Bergh, an art-restitution lawyer, and his somatic-therapist wife, Corinne, felt compelled to transform it into a ­cultural hub, platforming contemporary Moroccan artists and designers, and curating art events and creative retreats. —Paula Hardy.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Check Availability at Priceline.

    Sources indicate that set between the mountains and the sea, this smart family-friendly resort and discreet spa retreat was conceived and built by King Mohammed VI as a showcase for the artisanal skills and flair that are a cornerstone of Morocco’s cultural heritage. The Royal Mansour Tamuda Bay houses more than 2,000 works of art in an astounding showcase for Moroccan craftsmanship and artisanal skills. Set on a 700-meter private beachfront along the so-called Moroccan Riviera, it sits low within a landscaped garden scented with rosemary, sage lavender, and mint. While there are some substantial name resorts further along the coastline including Sofitel and Ritz Carlton, this the first home-grown luxury offering and stands head and shoulders above the others for its service (all staff are trained at Royal Mansour’s own hospitality school) and obsessive attention to detail, as well as its sustainable practices. It’s also open year-round for dedicated spa-goers who come for Longevity programs of varying time frames in the largest and most professional med spa in Northern Africa. —Catherine Fairweather.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    In a recent development, A shiny, super-sized proposition from Four Seasons, successfully incorporating beautiful Moroccan touches in the shared areas and sleek luxury in the private spaces. This would be an ideal three- or four-night stop for a spot of sightseeing and a lot of pampering as part of a wider Moroccan tour, with the city itself being a serene introduction to what is a very colorful and frenetic country. The true headliner here is the newly opened spa, which has a thorough menu and high-end treatments for every mood, with the opportunity to relax by the magnificent indoor pool afterwards. There’s an effortless blending of old and new, and a devotion to looking after the guest. Palatial, imposing, luxurious, with an impressive attention to detail, Four Seasons’ newest Moroccan property makes you feel like a modern day sultan. —Matt Charlton.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    According to recent reports, three years after opening La Sultana Marrakech in 2004, the owners sought a quieter, more intimate spot to unveil their second Moroccan hotel. The result was La Sultana’s beachy sanctuary of restorative wellness, slotted between acres of flourishing farmland and a tranquil lagoon sheltered from the roaring Atlantic. Sustainable, sea-to-table dining is central to the La Sultana experience, and seafood lovers will be glad to hear that oysters are the star dish, with five oyster beds scattered across the lagoon. All rooms have their own elegant personality, and with just 12 to choose from, the precision which has gone into each design is palpable. The Treehouse Suite is a personal favorite, centred around a real eucalyptus tree which permeates through the bedroom floor and ceiling. There’s a lovely cathedral-inspired spa exclusive to guests, with pool, hot tub, sauna, and five treatment rooms, as well as a nearly 150-foot infinity pool outside, seamlessly seeping into the sea at high tide. —Layla Quaedvlieg.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Sources indicate that the rocky sparseness of Morocco’s Agafay desert has long attracted travelers wanting a break from the sensory explosions of Marrakech. It’s an ideal landing spot for the Habitas group, which since 2016 has been setting up its minimalist, sustainable eco-retreats in places like Mexico, Namibia, and Saudi Arabia. Their oasis among the lunar dunes eschews bells and whistles in favor of communal vibes and engagement with nature—or “luxury for the soul,” as the founders call it. They've now applied their ethos to Agafay’s 41 Berber-inspired tents and lodges. Each en suite tent—solar-powered, with eco-bathrooms—embodies stylish pared-down-ness: no minibars or TVs, just wooden floors and earthy cream and ochre tones reminiscent of the regional rock.

    Weekenders escaping European cities sink into poufs and Berber rugs inside the communal glass-wrapped lounge. On the semi-open dining veranda, beneath raffia lamps, they tuck into lamb slow-cooked in the underground oven before knocking back market sangrias by the open-air bar, silhouetted against the Atlas Mountains and flame-red sunsets that give way to heavenly constellations. This is what travel is about—less guilt and more meaning amid tranquillity, good conversation, and cleansing nature. —Noo Saro-Wiwa.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    In a recent development, with a name as reputable as Nobu on the door, good service, and an even better restaurant offering are practically scribed into the brickwork. Marrakech is the brand's first foray into Africa, and its interiors remain respectful of the location, capturing a different kind of aesthetic that sets it apart from its Mediterranean cousins. The location is one to celebrate. From here, you can walk to the medina and the souks, or arrange drivers to take you further afield via the concierge, who suggests tours to the Atlas mountains, desert picnics, and cultural experiences like camel rides. The rooftop is as beautiful as the 360-degree views it offers, and watching the sun cast ombre shades of pink and orange across the sky before it sinks behind the horizon is best accompanied by a signature cocktail or a serving of mint tea—poured from an elaborate silver-tone pot, of course. Every bedroom is a suite bedecked in mahogany wood and rich furnishings. —Sarah Leigh Bannerman.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Recent findings suggest that at the Royal Mansour Marrakech, located inside the medina, the draw is privacy—its beautifully tiled riads have their own pools dotting lush gardens that are made for afternoon strolls. The palatial resort, founded by King Mohammed VI to showcase the best of Moroccan artistry and hospitality, was built over three years by 1,200 master craftsmen. It’s a swoon-worthy showpiece of Moroccan decorative art.

    In a recent development, each of the 53 individual three-story riads comprises a mini courtyard (with a canopy that automatically unfurls if rain is detected); a sumptuously appointed living room; an equally dazzling bedroom with silk-covered walls, hand-painted arched doorways, and generous MarocMaroc bath amenities; and a private rooftop terrace with a fireplace. Guests are tended to by a gracious staff, in particular a butler who appears silently through the riad’s kitchen service entry.

    Industry observers note that although Djemaa el Fna square is within walking distance, there’s much to keep you ensconced in this city sanctuary, including indoor and outdoor pools, a magnificent spa, and two superb restaurants, La Grande Table Marocaine and La Grande Table Française , as well as the indoor-outdoor La Table, which serves a formally presented breakfast and lunch by white-gloved staff. —Todd Plummer.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    It has been revealed that this is where Charlie Chaplin and Churchill chose to hole up, and Hitchcock filmed The Man Who Knew Too Much. Reinvigorated by designer Jacques Garcia, it had a spectacular reopening in 2009. Retreat from the hubbub to the huge gardens, with their beekeepers, lemon trees, secret ice-cream parlor, and the loveliest pool with a palm tree in the middle. The Sunday poolside brunch—tagines, grilled fish, pizza flatbreads—is excellent for hungry children, as is eating in Le Marocain to the sounds of a traditional oud (a bit like a lute). For a riad-style stay, there are three houses on the grounds, but the rooms with views out to the Koutoubia Mosque and over the rooftops of the Red City are the ones that give you the best sense of place. Pick up neon earthenware jugs, Berber-style rugs, and baskets at New York designer Martin Raffone’s MaisonLAB in Guéliz.

    Check Availability at Hotels.com.

    Recent findings suggest that all kasbahs are a kind of oasis of calm behind fortified walls, and Kasbah Tamadot is one of the very finest in Morocco. Its name means “soft breeze” in the local Berber language, evoking the reprieve it offers in the shadow of the Atlas Mountains. First built over a century ago as a home for a local governor, it became part of the Virgin Limited Edition Collection in 2005. Now reopened following substantial damage from the 2023 earthquake, Tamadot is a lavish yet quirky Amazigh castle with exquisite carved doors and intimate courtyards, secret passageways, and terraces of reflecting pools strewn with rose petals.

    In a recent development, it's furnished with the extraordinary collections of the previous owner, a Venetian antiquarian named Luciano Tempo, which were included when Richard Branson purchased the place. Huge bronze and wooden chests that might have carried Barbarossa’s loot stand in corners. In rambling gardens, pathways meander beneath trellises of jasmine while apple trees frame the cabanas around the swimming pool. In addition to atmospheric rooms in the old kasbah, accommodations offer a step-up in luxury with 10 glamorous Berber tents in the gardens and six luxurious riads (lovely three-bedroom suites with private pools). —Stanley Stewart.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Integrating opulence in just the right measure is a difficult task, but this five-star hotel (once home to the king's advisor) pulls it off perfectly. After you enter the building with its cream-colored walls, you’ll find yourself in the lobby, a luminous space with nearly 40-foot ceilings. It’s the first hint that this hotel does everything in style: from the eight acres of landscaped grounds to the dramatic lamps that illuminate the corridor leading to the Crudo restaurant and the photogenic swimming pool, where you’ll lose track of time under the Mediterranean sun.

    It has been revealed that the hotel’s 133 rooms are an amalgam of elements that celebrate the country’s craft traditions with fretwork wooden screens, mosaics, and bespoke fabrics created by local artisans. The Fairmont Tazi Palace’s massive wellness center includes 10 treatment rooms, a private spa, a solarium, a hammam you won’t want to leave, and sunny Andalusian-style gardens that lead to a secluded vitality pool. Let yourself unwind before refueling at one of the four restaurants, where ingredients are pulled from the hotel’s own orchard and kitchen garden. —Lidia González.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Industry observers note that it’s easy to forget what a game-changer El Fenn was when it opened two decades ago on the edge of the medina with just six jewel-toned bedrooms and a rooftop that felt like a fabulous house party. It stitched itself into the fabric of the Red City and redefined its aesthetic with color-clashing walls and lounges of thickly woven Berber and velvet fabrics, Moorish keyhole archways, and orange trees.

    Like the best hotels, it has moved—and expanded—with the times. Co-owner Vanessa Branson has gradually bought up the crumbling neighboring riads to create a wondrous labyrinth of 13 interconnected buildings, 3 pools, and 41 bedrooms in blush pinks, mustards, and acid yellows. Some have zellige tiles, others hand-stitched camel leather floors and carved wooden ceilings, all offset with pop art and bright contemporary installations.

    According to recent reports, I recently stayed in one of the “cozy” rooms, behind an ornate cedar door. Between the hand-plastered traditional tadelakt wall, contemporary dot painting, and mother-of-pearl chandelier, it’s nearly impossible to tell old from latest, a result of using local artisans, natural fabrics, and upcycled furniture. Amid the rooftop’s pool, sunbeds and pops of color, the old magic of Marrakech endures. —Chloe Sachdev.

    Connecting with nature in Morocco's beauty spot, where you can be as active or as laid-back as you like, all while enjoying the breathtaking backdrop of the Atlas Mountains. Just 20 minutes outside the heart of Marrakech, the landscape starts to change—countless olive groves, tall leafy palms, and fragrant argan and lemon trees. The distant views of the Atlas Mountains paint the scene, but it's the grand arch at the resort’s entrance that sets the tone of sheer majesty. Step through the iconic Fairmont swinging doors and you’re greeted by towering ceilings, marble accents, plush furnishings, and an endless sense of chic glamour.

    In a recent development, the main bar, Le Bar, dressed in a sleek black-and-gold scheme, feels like a scene straight out of a James Bond film. Jaw-dropping Moroccan chandeliers add to the extravagant spirit and five-star quality. Outside, 570 acres of lush green landscape await, showcasing Marrakech’s horticultural prowess. Home to an 18-hole golf course and a pampering spa, it’s the ultimate base for wellness seekers, romantic couples, families, and culture vultures keen to experience the crème de la crème of Marrakech’s idyllic rural scene.

    This rare palm-framed fantasyland near Ouarzazate, whose name translates from Arabic as “House of Dreams,” was conjured20 years ago, from the wild imagination of a Parisian creative. Thierry Teyssier re-envisaged the 200-year-old ochre kasbah and its rammed-earth ramparts to honor its Berber heritage with authenticity, elegance, and an unrivaled romance. Spells at the hideaway are more magical than ever, with the handful of rooms in the North African castle joined by spacious suites at the edge of the Louis Benech–landscaped grounds.

    Teyssier’s past lives as a theater actor and event planner keep him challenging traditional hospitality as a disrupter and storyteller: Every soul-stirring scene is art-directed and choreographed to enchant, with delicate, tactile interiors, seductive scents, and unexpected curios at every turn. Surrendering to Dar Ahlam’s rare rhythm is akin to participating in immersive theatre, with unprompted poolside pomegranate juices, candlelit Berber tents for secret suppers, and personally addressed hand-penned scrolls or other gifts at bedtime. Guests can explore vast desert-scapes by four-by-four, or let the staff plan a picnic in a villager’s vegetable garden. There is no lobby, restaurant, or bar, just beautiful spaces unfettered by telephones, menus, or minibars. —Juliet Kinsman.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    In a recent development, royal Mansour, owned by Morocco’s royal family, can be credited as one of Marrakech’s (if not Morocco’s) finest stays: a romantic riad, where luxury is distinctly of the old-world variety. Naturally, the announcement of a second location sent the travel industry into a titter. Heads up, though: Anyone expecting a mirror image of Royal Mansour Marrakech is going to be surprised. While the level of service and luxury at the fresh location (in the once-home of the 1953-built El Mansour hotel) follows the first property’s lead, the experience, and especially the aesthetic, is a departure. There are 149 rooms, with three categories of suites, and several “apartment” offerings.

    There are four restaurants: The brasserie serves delicious French classics, and at the sushi bar, chefs from Japan take on the task of bringing omakase to a Moroccan audience. For Moroccan food, head up to the 23rd floor. Just before sunset, the room of mirrors and gold comes alive in the light. Stick around for delicious sweet baghrir bread, fried spinach cheese briouat, and naturally, more tajines. The views over the city aren’t bad either. —Megan Spurrell.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    How we choose the best hotels in Morocco.

    Every hotel on this list has been selected independently by our editors and written by a Condé Nast Traveler journalist who knows the destination and has visited that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider properties across price points that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination, keeping design, location, service, and sustainability credentials top of mind.
